title: Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference
author: Horace He and Thinking Machines Lab (2025)
why: The clearest account of why temperature-0 output drifts: batch-variant reductions in matmul, attention and RMSNorm, and how batch-invariant kernels fix it.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
author: Kaplan et al. (2020)
why: Section 2.1 derives forward-pass FLOPs per token (≈ 2N plus an attention term) and the parameter count of a transformer layer by layer.

title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
author: Holtzman et al. (ICLR 2020)
why: Introduces nucleus (top-p) sampling and shows why greedy and pure sampling both produce poor text.

title: Attention Is All You Need
author: Vaswani et al. (NeurIPS 2017)
why: The original transformer: scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention and the block structure every modern LLM still follows.

title: The Illustrated Transformer
author: Jay Alammar (2018)
why: Step-by-step diagrams of self-attention, multi-head attention and the encoder–decoder stack; the gentlest way into the paper.

title: [1hr Talk] Intro to Large Language Models
author: Andrej Karpathy (2023)
why: An hour-long map of what an LLM is: pretraining, fine-tuning, sampling, scaling laws and the security problems that follow.

title: Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out
author: Andrej Karpathy (2023)
why: Builds a small GPT in PyTorch line by line, so tokens, attention and the decode loop stop being abstractions.
